text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of text, such as books, websites and articles. This training data helps them answer questions, write texts and translate languages. To get good results, users often use prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. However, LLMs also have limits. They can make mistakes, give wrong information, or reflect biases found in their training data. For this reason, it is always wise to check important answers carefully.
